messages.subject: quick nan-error related question

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: quick nan-error related question
parts:
The N4stan5agrad3varE doesn't mean anything I don't think. The gamma_log() function received a nan value on input. If that doesn't happen on the first function evaluation, then it usually means the previous gradient calculation went nan somehow and then the next proposal went nan because it is a function of the previous gradient.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] quick nan-error related question
parts:
> On Oct 31, 2014, at 3:05 PM, Alp Kucukelbir <akucu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> hi folks,
>
> does an error like this mean something specific to any of you?
>
> "
> Exception: stan::prob::gamma_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable[1] is nan:0, but must not be nan!
> Diagnostic information:
> Dynamic exception type: St12domain_error
> std::exception::what: stan::prob::gamma_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable[1] is nan:0, but must not be nan!
> "

There's a sampling statement y ~ gamma(alpha,beta) or function call gamma_log(y,alpha,beta)
where y is NaN. Usually this will only happen if you try to use a local variable before
it's defined, or divide 0 by 0, or subtract infinity from infinity or the like.

Are you up to date with the latest release? I think the : went away,
but "nan:0" is just the value:adjoint, and all adjoints are initialized
to 0 for autodiff variables.
> i'm trying to pinpoint where things are going awry. should "N4stan5agrad3varE" mean something to me?

C++ mangles names, that's telling you that the scalar type is
stan::agrad::var.

Daniel's working on making these messages more interpretable right now.

- Bob
